free_tier.stated: The service is shut down. 'XS Usenet has shut down - but your Usenet service continues without interruption. All accounts have been moved to EasyUsenet.' The website and ordering system are closed.

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap is published; the unit of retrieval is a Usenet article, ~750 KB by convention, so a 1 TiB month is roughly 1.4 million article fetches
per_object_cap.notes: an article size is a protocol convention, not a vendor number

retention.stated: Not applicable: no new accounts are sold. Existing accounts keep their expiry date on the EasyUsenet infrastructure.

egress.terms: Not applicable; the ordering system is closed

interface_detail: NNTP over TLS on port 563; no HTTP or object API exists for the download path, so the client drives it through SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav
tooling: SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav over NNTP/TLS; any newsreader works because the protocol is the same everywhere, and no provider SDK is needed
chaining: Nothing composes: the capacity moved to EasyUsenet, which is the Abavia brand a client should price instead.
limits_note: No limits apply to a service that no longer signs up customers. The last published terms were a soft 5 TB/month ceiling on unlimited plans with speed cut to 40 Mbit above it, per the r/usenet map.
binding_note: Nothing binds because nothing is sold. A reader who needs this capacity must go to EasyUsenet, which inherited the accounts.

identity_cost.detail: Registration is closed. Existing credentials were migrated unchanged to reader.easyusenet.com.

reliability_note: Shut down after 15 years, citing staff shortages; accounts moved to EasyUsenet with the same username and password and a new hostname. The VPN product was suspended and set to close on August 31, with refunds for unused time.
confidence_note: The shutdown notice is the vendor's own page, read today. The fetch reported no upstream status, so the page content is the evidence rather than an HTTP code.

evidence.proved: 'XS Usenet has shut down'; 'All accounts have been moved to EasyUsenet'; new server reader.easyusenet.com; 'Since starting in 2009 as the first freemium Usenet provider'
Xsusenet listed as an Abavia reseller with 'soft limits (5tb per month) ... above 5TB speed will be capped to 40Mbit'

notes: The interesting part is the epitaph: the first freemium Usenet provider in 2009 is gone in 2026, and its free-tier model went with it. That is the direction of travel's main question.
